title: Settings › AI accounts connects Kimi, GLM and Qwen with a pasted API key: the broker proves the key on a cheap vendor door before sealing it, sorts refusals into key / plan / vendor, never keeps an unproven key, and tells the client each vendor's sign-in kind; the client draws the key row and maps the door's refusals
steps: Common setup: none — pure unit run, no stand, no database, no network (vendor fetch is a test double).
S1: From the TCH checkout run the command in `run.cmd`.
S2: Read the result of each test named in `run.tests`.
expect: Every test named in run.tests reports ok.

selectors.function: apps/tracy-web/src/seat-plan/wire/api-key.js probeKey; apps/tracy-web/src/seat-plan/broker.js connectKey, signInOf; packages/ui/tracy-model-plan/src/client/plan-doors.ts connectKey, signInFor

fence: A pasted key reaches the vault only after the vendor's cheap door (GET /models, or Z.ai's quota door) accepted it; a 401 (for Qwen: on both regions), any 403 or plan/quota refusal, and a vendor outage come back as three distinct codes (key, plan, vendor); a 403 on a chat turn keeps the stored key so the client never shows 'wrong key' for an outage; the stored blob is {kind:'key',v:1,apiKey} with subject = full SHA-256 of the key and label 'API key …' + last 4; the client takes a vendor's sign-in kind from the server's status answer and keeps its own table only for vendors older servers know.

tests: a good key is proven on /models and kept as a key blob with a hashed identity
a good key is proven on the quota door and kept as a key blob with a hashed identity
a rejected key is a key error
a rejected key is a key error, whether Z.ai says so in the status or only in the body
a key without a membership is a plan error, not a bad key
a key with no coding plan or balance is a plan error
a key whose account is out of quota or in arrears is a plan error
kimi down or slow is a vendor error
Z.ai down or slow is a vendor error
DashScope down or slow is a vendor error
another region is a second probe away: a Beijing key refused abroad is kept with the endpoint that took it
a key refused by both regions is a key error; any other answer is not
any 403 is an access refusal (plan), never a wrong key
